missing_items: Printed objectives (resources, methods, how to select a sample, types of samples)
Key terms list (primary resources, secondary resources, method of mass population, method of sample, biased choice, random choice sample, random sample, layer sample)
Intro statement that data collection is a key phase for accurate statistical inference and decision making
Method is determined by aim and size of the statistical society
Example: students of a school as a statistical society whose value is the student
Disadvantages: needs long time, great efforts, costs much money
Method depends on selecting a sample from the statistical society it represents
Research is conducted on the sample and outcomes are generalized to the whole society
Introductory heading on how to select samples and the conditions required for a sample
Example: analyzing a maths lesson test using only a group of students who studied the topic is not random selection
Lead-in that simple random and layer samples are the most important types of random samples
Instruction to repeat pressing = so numbers appear successively
Layer sample example: 400 persons, male:female 3:2, sample of 50, so 30 males and 20 females chosen randomly
Reference to MOE website for more exercises

meter.record: uv run meter_run.py record --book prep3-parallel --stage S2-S4,S8 --run <runId>
meter.by_stage: uv run meter_run.py summary --book prep3-parallel --by phase
meter.by_lesson: uv run meter_run.py summary --book prep3-parallel --by lesson
meter.note: Phase titles start with their stage (S2, S3, S4, S8), so `--by phase` is the per-stage cost; every label carries the lesson slug (S3:blind:<slug>:1), so `--by lesson` is the per-lesson cost.
